name: Optimize VerFSNext write speed while preserving read/consistency/dedup

description: Use packs.sync_data() instead of sync_all() before commit — reduces fsync from 4 syscalls (2 files × data+meta) to 2 syscalls (data only). sync_data guarantees data + size metadata, and index is rebuildable from pack records on crash via rebuild_index_if_missing.

asi.hypothesis: sync_data is sufficient for crash ordering — pack data on disk before metadata commit. sync_all's metadata flush (timestamps, sizes) is unnecessary since both files are rebuildable from pack records.

description: Remove redundant seek(SeekFrom::End(0)) in pack append — use size_bytes directly which is tracked under lock. Saves one syscall per chunk written.

asi.hypothesis: active.size_bytes under the write lock equals file position at end for O_APPEND files. No need for an extra seek syscall.

description: Save data copy optimization — avoid cloning WriteOp data in apply_queued_batch by taking ownership of the Vec via mem::take instead

asi.hypothesis: Avoid one unnecessary Vec clone per write reduces memory bandwidth pressure

description: ALL 9 integration tests pass including git_clone_comfyui_manager_regression (B002 regression test) and full ComfyUI benchmark

Pre-compute batch timestamp once per retry attempt in apply_batch — pass (sec,nsec) through apply_single_write_in_txn → commit_prepared_write_in_txn instead of calling SystemTime::now() per inode group

asi.hypothesis: Compute SystemTime::now() once per batch attempt instead of once per inode-group. Saves ~N clock_gettime syscalls per commit batch where N is the number of inode groups. Theoretical saving is 20-30ns per syscall, meaningful under sustained concurrent write load.

description: Buffer index entries in pending_index Vec — flush to index_file in a single write_all() during sync() instead of writing each 44-byte entry individually

asi.hypothesis: Buffer index entries in memory and flush in a single write_all during sync instead of writing each 44-byte entry individually. Saves one write syscall per index entry. index_cache is updated immediately so reads work correctly.

description: Skip KV extent scan in prepare_write_plan when inode.size == 0 — new or truncated files have no extents, avoiding a read transaction per write

asi.hypothesis: Skip the KV extent range scan in prepare_write_plan when inode.size == 0. Newly created files and truncated-to-zero files have no extents, so the scan always returns empty. Saves one KV read transaction per write to a new file.
